interactions.summary: Jiang answers his own question emphatically, saying Dante knew the poem would matter and pointing to the fact that he died right after finishing the Divine Comedy.
Students answer that Dante endures because the poem treats eternal human topics and because people will always seek God-sized questions whose answers arrive only at death.

Jiang closes the morning by saying the eternal and the true are recognized in the heart and intuition, not proved logically, and that what is truly eternal stretches both into the future and back into the past.
The session breaks into room-management chatter and fragmentary self-introductions after Jiang ends the morning session.

speaker_notes.note: These segments appear to be off-stage or ambient room audio during the break rather than substantive lecture content.

claims.claim: Jiang asserts that Dante knew the Divine Comedy would matter and immediately ties that certainty to the biographical fact that he died right after finishing it.
claims.temporal_scope: Jiang historical and interpretive claim stated on 2026-06-15 about Dante's completed poem.

claims.claim: A student argues that Dante's topics are eternal and human, which is why people may still be learning from them even thousands of years later.
Another student says people will always remain curious about God and that such questions are not fully answered until death.
Jiang says that if you know in your heart what is eternal and true, you know it extends both forward into the future and backward into the past.
Jiang says this recognition of the eternal cannot be logically explained and instead is accomplished through faith and intuition.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang treats Dante's death immediately after finishing the poem as evidence that he knew what he had completed.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Right after he finished the Divine Comedy, he died
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the packet a hard biographical edge instead of leaving the discussion at the level of vague posterity.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang tells the class to look into the heart to know what is eternal and true.
signature_moments.source_phrase: if you just look into your heart
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's central method claim: the eternal is recognized through inner attunement rather than analytic proof.

signature_moments.moment: The true is described as something that simultaneously extends into the future and back into the past.
signature_moments.source_phrase: extend into the future as well as extend back in the past
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It compresses Jiang's theory of timeless truth into a memorable temporal image that later reads will need to preserve.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: For Jiang, what the heart can recognize as true across both past and future rather than only in one historical moment.
Named by Jiang as the mode through which the eternal is grasped when logic cannot finish the work.
Paired with faith as the faculty that recognizes timeless truth without reducing it to formal proof.

chronology_notes.note: This packet binds a historical endpoint in Dante's life to Jiang's morning-session argument that genuine truth spans past and future; it adds temporal framing within the June 15 lecture but does not update Jiang across sources.

uncertainty_notes.note: The transcript turns into break chatter and repeated names, so those segments should not be mined for public-facing claims.
